tldr: ReMA is a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework that decouples LLM reasoning into a high-level meta-thinking agent and a low-level reasoning agent, enabling LLMs to learn to think about thinking and outperforming single-agent RL baselines on complex reasoning tasks.
contributions: Introducing ReMA, the first framework to formally define and optimize a multi-agent meta-thinking reasoning process (MAMRP) through multi-agent reinforcement learning
Decoupling reasoning into hierarchical agents: a high-level meta-thinking agent for strategic oversight and a low-level reasoning agent for detailed execution
Extending ReMA to multi-turn interaction settings with turn-level ratio and parameter sharing to improve training efficiency
Demonstrating superior out-of-distribution generalization on mathematical benchmarks and LLM-as-a-Judge tasks across multiple backbone models
methods: ReMA formulates reasoning as a Markov Game between two LLM agents: a high-level agent π_h generates meta-thoughts (plans, monitors, revises strategy), and a low-level agent π_l executes detailed problem-solving under those instructions. Training uses REINFORCE++/GRPO with aligned reward functions. For single-turn MAMRP, two separate model copies are used. For multi-turn MAMRP, parameter sharing is adopted (both agents share weights θ, distinguished only by role-specific system prompts) to enable larger batch sizes and avoid GPU swap inefficiencies. A turn-level ratio is introduced instead of token-level ratio to stabilize multi-turn training by clipping at the turn level rather than per token.
results: Single-turn ReMA outperforms all baselines on average, with a maximum improvement of 6.68% on mathematical benchmarks and 8.49% on LLM-as-a-Judge benchmarks. Notable OOD gains include +20% on AMC23 (Llama-3-8B-Instruct), +13.33% on AIME24 (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct), and +14.23% on RewardBench970 (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct). Larger LLMs (Llama-3.1-8B) adapt meta-thinking strategies based on problem difficulty, while smaller LLMs (Llama-3.2-1B) collapse to the simplest EMPTY action. RL under meta-thinking achieves the best learning dynamics and generalizes better to hard problems compared to SFT or RL from base.
limitations: Single-turn MAMRP lacks ability for immediate, fine-grained cognitive switching during reasoning, limiting effectiveness on complex long-horizon planning tasks
RL training on instruction-tuned LLMs yields smaller accuracy gains compared to base models, due to higher initial performance and relatively fixed output distributions
Smaller LLMs struggle to maintain valid JSON formatting while exploring diverse reasoning strategies, causing convergence to simpler outputs
